title: Kenyan Viazi Karai
author: Chef Amina Hassan

relatedDish.note: KEN116 is a Street Food category entry for Viazi Karai. The primary recipe with full heritage, regional map, and cultural notes is KEN017 (Authentic Kenyan Viazi Karai). Both describe the same Mombasa street food classic.

desc: Viazi Karai — Mombasa's most beloved street food. Boiled potato halves coated in spiced gram flour batter and deep-fried until golden and crispy, served with tamarind coconut chutney. See KEN017 for the full recipe with complete heritage.
longDesc: Viazi Karai is the coastal version of bhajia — where bhajia uses thin potato slices, viazi karai uses boiled potato halves, creating a more substantial snack with a soft, yielding interior beneath the crispy batter. The tamarind coconut chutney served alongside is as important as the potato itself.
steps: Boil potato halves in salted water for 12—15 minutes until just tender. Drain and cool completely.
Make batter: combine gram flour, rice flour, spices, and salt. Whisk in water to a thick, coating batter.
Make chutney: blend tamarind, coconut, sugar, garlic, coriander, and water until smooth.
Dip each potato half in batter. Fry for 3—4 minutes until deep golden.
Drain and serve immediately with chutney.
chefTips: Cool potatoes completely before battering — warm potatoes cause batter to slide off.
The batter must be thick enough to coat and cling.
commonMistakes: Thin batter — does not create a proper crust.
